water: Water regularly through the first year. Established plants cope with ordinary dry spells.

uses: Specimen · shrub borders · winter interest · wildlife gardens

pollination: not applicable; grown as an ornamental. Hazels are wind-pollinated and need a different hazel nearby to set nuts

resilience: Hardy, but late frost and cold wind can scorch new leaves; dislikes waterlogging and drought. Pests: aphids; prone to verticillium wilt and coral spot.
uses: Specimen tree · borders · woodland edge · Japanese-style gardens · large containers when young
foliage: deciduous; deeply divided, usually seven-lobed dark purple-red leaves

hardinessNote: Very hardy (H6) and survives very cold winters across the UK, roughly -20 to -15°C.
visual: Tiny flat-topped bun of dense, soft needle-like foliage, pale green new shoots maturing deep green · deep reddish-bronze in winter
water: Water regularly in its first year and never let pots dry out; established plants need water only in long dry spells.
prune: No routine pruning needed. If needed, trim lightly in spring to keep the shape.
toxicity: No reports of serious harm from eating it, but the foliage and resin may irritate sensitive skin, so wear gloves when handling or trimming.
cvs: 'Globosa Nana' – larger dome · 'Vilmoriniana' – compact globe, bronzes in winter · 'Elegans' – tall, soft juvenile foliage · 'Sekkan-sugi' – cream-tipped growth · 'Spiralis' – twisted foliage
resilience: Extremely slow; less hardy than most Cryptomeria and prone to sun scorch. Dislikes cold winds and drought. Pests: few; red spider mite if stressed.
uses: Rock gardens · alpine troughs · containers · Japanese-style planting · bonsai
foliage: evergreen; short, densely packed needle-like leaves forming a tight bun, bronzing in winter

uses: Borders · containers · low informal hedging · foliage contrast · scented planting near paths

pollination: not applicable; grown for foliage and flower, not fruit
